question: The smallest structure with a hidden excess has seven knots, mixes parity and not-all-equal knots and has no distinction held three times. Can ordinary growth, with a law given to each knot, make such a structure from a part of it, or make any structure that has a hidden excess once the setting birth is supplied?
inputs: The recorded growth operator, sources, draws and structures the pre-registration names; its seeds.
forbidden_inputs: Any definition changed after a value is seen; any outcome of this study before the freeze.
primary_observable: The items named under 'Runs and stop rule' of the pre-registration.
comparators_or_controls: Ordinary growth on the same starts; the code checks of row G.
resource_budget: Each run under ten minutes and 12 GB on one CPU process.
first_executable_signal: Row G of the predictions table.
decision_rule: Each prediction is judged by its 'Fails when' column.
stop_rule: One script builds the targets and founder starts, one grows and tests T1, one runs T2. The study stops when every target and every draw in the bounds is done. It reports the counts of founder starts grown and skipped, of stages and law assignments tested, and of observer choices in T2, and the reason each seven-knot founder start fails.
nonclaims: An exploratory study on named samples and bounded sizes. A rival growth law is a scaffold and not the model; a census is finite and proves no all-size statement.
